response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, f.rebtotal, (f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0) AS relgap FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink), g AS (SELECT orderslink, ordertune, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG(relgap) AS avg_relative_gap FROM j GROUP BY orderslink, ordertune), o AS (SELECT AVG(rebtotal) AS overall_avg FROM j) SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_relative_gap, g.avg_rebate - o.overall_avg AS above_overall_avg FROM g CROSS JOIN o WHERE g.avg_rebate > o.overall_avg ORDER BY above_overall_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The overall average rebate is the average of rebtotal over all fee rows that match an order (row-level, not an average of group averages).
Fees with feerate = 0 get a NULL relative gap (division by zero avoided via NULLIF), so they are ignored in the average gap but still count in the average rebate.
orders.recordvault is unique per order, so the join does not duplicate fee rows.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the mean of the per-group (orderslink, ordertune) average rebates, not the row-level average.
